Small Helper Functions for Data Catalog Access

Source: R/metadata_helpers.R
catalogs.Rd

A suite of small helper functions designed to interact with and retrieve essential metadata from various international organization data repositories (catalogs). These functions standardize the process of obtaining lists of available data access codes, collections, country codes, and latest entries from specified sources.

Usage

catalogs(show = TRUE)

access_codes(catalog)

collections(catalog)

country_codes(catalog)

latest_entries(catalog, limit = NULL)

metadata(catalog, id)

Arguments

show

Logical. If TRUE (default), prints the supported catalogs to the console. The catalog table is returned invisibly either way.

catalog

A required character string specifying the name of the data catalog (e.g., "fao", "wb") from which to retrieve metadata.

limit

A positive integer number, applicable only to latest_entries, indicating the maximum number of results (data entries) to return. If NULL or omitted, a default limit set by the API will be used.

id

A required study identifier. Accepts either the numeric Study ID (integer, e.g., 101) or the character Study ID Number (string, e.g., "ALB_2012_LSMS_v01_M_v01_A_PUF"). These values are typically returned in the search results from search_catalog(), latest_entries() or data_files().

Value

  • catalogs: Invisibly, a data frame with one row per supported catalog and the columns catalog, name, home and api.

  • access_codes: A data frame of the data access types, with columns such as id, type and title.

  • collections: A data frame of collections, with columns such as id, repositoryid and title.

  • country_codes: A data frame of country codes, with columns such as countryid, name and iso.

  • latest_entries: A data frame of the most recently added studies, with columns such as id, idno, title, nation, created, changed and url.

  • metadata: A list with the study description. Its main parts are doc_desc (about the documentation) and study_desc (about the study itself).

Column names come from each catalog's API, so they can differ slightly between catalogs. If a catalog returns no records, a warning is issued and the result is empty. Network failures, HTTP errors and non-JSON replies raise an error.

Details

All functions require a valid catalog code (see the Supported Catalogs section) and return their results in a standardized format. An unknown code stops with an error that lists the supported catalogs.

Each request waits up to 30 seconds and is attempted up to three times before it fails. If a catalog replies with something other than JSON, for example a block page for automated clients, the function stops with a clear message. Use set_user_agent to change the user agent sent with requests.

Catalogs differ in what they publish. For example, ihsn has no collections, so collections("ihsn") warns that it returned 0 collections and gives an empty result.

Supported Catalogs

The catalog argument must be one of the following short codes (case-insensitive) corresponding to the respective microdata repository. The list is sorted alphabetically by code.

  • "df": Data First (https://www.datafirst.uct.ac.za)

  • "erf": Economic Research Forum (https://erfdataportal.com)

  • "fao": Food and Agriculture Organization (https://microdata.fao.org)

  • "ihsn": International Household Survey Network (https://catalog.ihsn.org)

  • "kenya": Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (https://statistics.knbs.or.ke/nada/index.php)

  • "unhcr": United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (https://microdata.unhcr.org)

  • "wb": The World Bank (https://microdata.worldbank.org)

  • "who": World Health Organization Health Information Systems (https://apps.who.int/healthinfo/systems/surveydata/index.php/catalog)

  • "zambia": Zambia Statistics Agency (https://nada.zamstats.gov.zm)

See also

The main search function: search_catalog; study files and variables: data_files; the user agent setting: set_user_agent

Author

Gutama Girja Urago

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# --- Examples for Supported Catalogs ---

# 1. Data First (df): Get available access codes.
df_codes <- access_codes("df")

# 2. Economic Research Forum (erf): Get latest data entries (limited to 5).
erf_latest <- latest_entries("erf", limit = 5)

# 3. Food and Agriculture Organization (fao): Get available collections.
fao_collections <- collections("fao")

# 4. International Household Survey Network (ihsn): Get supported country codes.
ihsn_countries <- country_codes("ihsn")

# 5. Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (kenya): Get available collections.
kenya_collections <- collections("kenya")

# 6. United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (unhcr): Get available collections.
unhcr_collections <- collections("unhcr")

# 7. The World Bank (wb): Get supported country codes.
wb_countries <- country_codes("wb")

# 8. World Health Organization HIS (who): Get available access codes.
who_codes <- access_codes("who")

# 9. Zambia Statistics Agency (zambia): Get latest entries (limit 10).
zambia_latest <- latest_entries("zambia", limit = 10)

# Example for the metadata function (requires a study ID)
wb_study_metadata <- metadata("wb", id = 8098)
str(wb_study_metadata)
}
